identity.title: Live-cell imaging reveals two modes of TERRA association with telomeres and the dynamics of TERRA R-loops.

content.abstract: Telomeres are transcribed into TERRA long non-coding RNAs. When associating with telomeres, TERRA can regulate telomere maintenance by semiconservative DNA replication, telomerase and homology-directed repair (HDR). In addition, TERRA alters telomeric structure and protein composition. Yet, the molecular mechanisms and dynamics by which TERRA associates with telomeres remain elusive. To investigate TERRA-telomere interactions, we combine PP7 stem-loop TERRA tagging, genome editing and live-cell imaging. Using a deep-learning method for spot detection and single-particle tracking analysis, we demonstrate that TERRA associates with telomeres through two distinct modes. On one hand, TERRA interacts frequently and transiently with the telomeric shelterin protein TRF2. On the other hand, TERRA engages in long-lasting interactions which persist from seconds to several minutes forming R-loops with telomeric DNA. TERRA R-loops preferentially occur at short telomeres, and their formation requires factors involved in HDR, but not TRF2. Altogether, we reveal two parallel mechanisms of TERRA recruitment to telomeres, which differ substantially in their dynamics and structure, and we elucidate the dynamics of telomeric R-loops. Our findings provide a framework for understanding TERRA-triggered telomere functions during aging and carcinogenesis.
